clue.text: Ratty pair, perhaps, before rainstorm

indicators.note: before places the first rearranged piece ahead of the second in the answer
perhaps hints that the word pair may be rearranged into another order
storm, tacked onto rain, suggests those four letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Two bad-tempered people come along just ahead of a heavy downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratty' looks like 'irritable' but is the Water Rat of The Wind in the Willows, a riverbank dweller. 'perhaps' turns PAIR into RIPA; 'storm' turns RAIN into RIAN, read out of the single word 'rainstorm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty in Kenneth Grahame's story lives on the riverbank, and the adjective describes anything living beside a river.

clue.text: Beefier, being more highly-seasoned

explanation.surface: A dish made beefier by being spiced more heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefier person is more powerful and muscular; a more highly-seasoned dish has a more pungent taste.

clue.text: Careless overuse of poets' works

indicators.note: careless suggests the letters of overuse are handled sloppily and scattered

explanation.surface: Sloppy repetition spoils what the poets have written.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word names the complete body of output of a writer or artist.

clue.text: Smart cycle purchase?

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cycle, as in cycles per second
purchase can mean leverage or grip, so a lever gives purchase

explanation.surface: A bright idea for buying a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying, but here it is the mechanical sense: a firm hold or leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and quick-witted are synonyms for intelligent.

clue.text: Merry wives left to pirouette

indicators.note: merry, as in tipsy, suggests the letters of wives reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Tipsy wives are left spinning round on the dance floor, a nod to The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirouette is to spin round on one spot, as a swivel chair turns.

clue.text: Referee as informer

explanation.surface: A match official who also tells tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee blows a whistle to stop play; an informer exposes wrongdoing at an organisation.

clue.text: Conduct no worse than usual in our orbit?

explanation.surface: Behaviour that is merely ordinary, as seen from our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ordinary human behaviour, accepted as normal; read literally, it is the path the Earth travels round the sun.

clue.text: Bartering, unusual practice on rig

indicators.note: unusual signals that practice and on rig are arranged in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Trading goods in an odd way out on an oil platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanging goods in return for other goods is giving and taking in turn, i.e. mutual exchange.

clue.text: Energetic person required for the Monday shift

indicators.note: shift tells us to move the letters of Monday about

explanation.surface: A lively worker is needed to cover the start-of-week rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work rota, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tireless, forceful person is likened to an electrical generator.

clue.text: Long live cove turning out for an oral examination

parts.note: viva is the Italian and Spanish cry meaning long live

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters of cove are turned into a different order

explanation.surface: A cheer for a chap who shows up to be tested in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' is British slang for a fellow, though here it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by the living voice, and names a spoken test, as for a university degree.

clue.text: Neither of the poets gives name to ring road

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
R is the abbreviation for road on maps

explanation.surface: Neither poet gives a ring road its name.
explanation.walkthrough: Poets often write 'nor ... nor' where prose has 'neither ... nor', so 'Neither of the poets' is a poetic usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse the conjunction can open a pair of negatives where everyday English uses neither.

clue.text: Likely to occur soon in this part of the sea

definitions.meaning: only in the phrase 'in the ___' does the word mean imminent

explanation.surface: Something about to happen out in a distant stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible sea far from shore is the original sense; 'in the ___' therefore means coming soon.

clue.text: Deerstalker pieces, up, induce panic in listeners

indicators.note: in shows one word placed inside the other, panic going into the listeners

parts.note: listeners are the organs we hear with
a flap is a state of panic

explanation.surface: Raised hat flaps make the hearers fret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' refers to the flaps of a deerstalker hat, which tie up over the crown; it and 'induce' act as linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: The deerstalker, the cap of Sherlock Holmes, has folding side pieces that cover the ears.

clue.text: Means of cooling enthusiast

explanation.surface: A way of keeping cool, and a keen supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held or electric device moves air to cool you; a supporter or devotee of a team or star.

clue.text: Conspicuous things, black eyes!

explanation.surface: Prominent objects, and a couple of bruised eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that gleam stand out brightly; slang names bruised eye sockets the same way.

clue.text: Age of moderation

indicators.note: of indicates the answer is drawn from within the word moderation

explanation.surface: A time of restraint and temperance.
explanation.definitionFit: An age and an epoch are both long periods of history.

clue.text: Overnight accommodation with neat compartment for hats

parts.note: B and B, bed and breakfast, is overnight lodging
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox is neat

explanation.surface: A night's lodging comes with tidy hat storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but is the archaic word for cattle, here OX.
explanation.definitionFit: A light cardboard box was originally made to hold collar bands, and later to hold hats.

clue.text: This provides an escort for father, we hear

definitions.note: spoken aloud, for father sounds like forefather, a predecessor in the family line

indicators.note: provides suggests the letters of an escort can be made to supply a new word

explanation.surface: Something that lays on a chaperone for dad, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for father, we hear' is the definition by sound: it is heard as 'forefather'. 'This provides' tells you to rearrange AN ESCORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A forefather is someone from whom you are descended, a forebear.

clue.text: Difficulty in discerning character of Lydia's ex, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of Lydia's ex may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Lydia's former partner may have trouble reading letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like personality, but means a written letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A learning disability affecting reading means letters and words are hard to make out.

clue.text: Endless deficit toppling to earth in a pile

indicators.note: toppling suggests the shortened word falls over into a new arrangement
endless means the word deficit loses its final letter

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: An unending shortfall collapses into a heap on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts DEFICIT to DEFICI, and 'toppling' rearranges that into EDIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a large imposing building, the same as a grand structure.

clue.text: Like Janus and the pair confronted

parts.note: a pair is two
to confront someone is to face them

explanation.surface: Janus and the couple came face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: Janus is the Roman god with two faces, looking forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god is shown with heads looking both ways, so he is literally double-sided, a word also meaning deceitful.

clue.text: Fleur-de-lis decoration of one in last

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: final means last
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lily emblem decorating the last of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament on top of a spire or post, often shaped like a fleur-de-lis, is an architectural crowning piece.

clue.text: So rich in pieces for singing groups

indicators.note: in pieces says the letters of so rich are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: So wealthy as to buy pieces for vocal ensembles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' looks like pieces of music for singing, but 'in pieces' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of singers, as in a church or cathedral, are vocal ensembles.

clue.text: Price, a pound, of ribs

parts.note: a price is a cost
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The cost of a pound of spare ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the anatomical term relating to the ribs, from Latin costa.

clue.text: Diamonds set in classic eardrops

indicators.note: set in tells us the answer is placed within the words classic eardrops

explanation.surface: Gems mounted in elegant earrings.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for diamonds likens the clear gems to frozen water.

clue.text: To win against odds, bachelor has to stop telephoning

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
to ring off is to end a phone call

explanation.surface: A single man must hang up to triumph against the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'ring off' is British for hanging up the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull off a difficult feat is to accomplish it despite the odds.

clue.text: Endless variety of coin money

indicators.note: endless means the synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: a species is a type or variety

explanation.surface: An endless range of coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in the form of coins rather than notes is called by this Latin-derived name.

clue.text: Wooden settlement that shows our position

parts.note: wooden, meaning lifeless and stiff, can mean dead
a reckoning is the settlement of an account

explanation.surface: A stiff bill to settle reveals where we stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Navigators without instruments work out position from speed, heading and time elapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigational method estimates a ship's location from known speed, course and time.
